answer: Sybil resistance can come from trust-graph distance: new identities start with zero standing and gain it only through endorsements that trace back, via short random walks, to long-established agents. A velvet rope of short paths keeps strangers out: a plume of fresh aliases with no genuine links to the trusted core stays distant no matter how many are spun up, and the old fable that sheer numbers equal influence fails, because forging hundreds of real, independent trust edges costs far more than the reward any single fake identity can earn.
